parsed.rationale: The two protocols `AsyncNotificationMessage` (production, `is_test=false`) and `MockNotificationMessage` (test fixture, `is_test=true`) serve structurally similar but intentionally distinct roles: the production protocol in `Shared/Core/Sources/Core/Observation/AsyncMessage.swift` defines the real notification-message contract, while `MockNotificationMessage` in `Shared/Core/Sources/CoreTesting/_Plant_MockNotificationMessage.swift` is a test-support plant/mock that deliberately mirrors that shape. The single differing slot — `makeMessage:(_ notification: sending Notification) -> Self?` vs `makeMessage:(_ notification: Notification) -> Self?` — indicates the test version uses the `sending` ownership annotation, which is a meaningful semantic divergence appropriate for a test double. Collapsing these into a shared PAT hierarchy would couple production and test infrastructure unnecessarily and risk leaking test-only concurrency semantics into the production protocol.
